title: Facet proposal packet
description: The concepts the operator chooses between and the production plan they approve, written by the director with the producer to artifacts/proposal_packet.json. It is the last point where a change of direction is free: no asset is made and no paid tool is called before the operator approves it. Paid steps carry the tool's credit note.

concept_options.description: Two to four genuinely different concepts, three by default. No two share a structure or hook pattern, each rests on different findings, and one takes a creative risk; three titles for one idea are one concept.

selected_concept.description: The concept chosen, with any mixing the operator asked for.

concept_id.description: Id of the chosen concept in concept_options.

rationale.description: Why this concept: the operator's choice or your recommendation, and the reason.

modifications.description: Changes the operator asked for, such as the hook of one concept with the look of another.

paid_steps.description: Every step that calls a paid tool, each with the free alternative beside it. Empty when the plan is fully free.

approval.description: Always asked: present, stop, end the turn, then record the answer here. An earlier go-ahead does not cover this approval.

id.description: c1, c2, c3 and so on.

hook.description: The opening line: under 20 words, opens an information gap, grounded in a named finding. Never "In this video we'll…".

narrative_structure.description: A structure id from the pipeline (pipeline_describe), such as hook-build-payoff, or a narrative form: analogy, problem_solution, journey, debate, myth_busting, timeline, comparison, tutorial, story, data_narrative.

visual_approach.description: The treatment: how it looks, sounds and moves, specific enough to guide the scene plan.

suggested_playbook.description: A style id (clean-professional, flat-motion-graphics, minimalist-diagram, premium-minimalist, anime-ghibli), or custom when the look is designed for this subject.

target_audience.description: The audience segment this concept serves best.

key_points.description: Concrete claims the video will prove, not topics.

core_message.description: The one thing the viewer remembers tomorrow.

cta.description: Call to action, specific and relevant.

grounded_in.description: The research_brief findings this concept rests on.

audience_effect.description: What the audience should understand, feel or do afterwards, in the stance's terms.

keeps_from_reference.description: Reference-driven work: at least one element kept from the reference (pacing, structure, tone, hook style).

changes_from_reference.description: Reference-driven work: at least one element changed (angle, subject, treatment, platform), with why the change is better.

reuse_strategy.description: Animation: the motifs, layout system, transition family and type hierarchy that hold the piece together.

production_plan.description: The plan the operator approves. render_runtime, composition_mode, renderer_family and delivery_promise are locked here; later stages carry them unchanged and change them only with the operator's agreement.

style.description: A style id, or custom when the visual identity is designed for this subject (described in art_direction and taste_profile). Use a preset only when it honestly fits.

render_runtime.description: The engine. remotion: React compositions (Explainer scenes, data charts, word captions, TalkingHead, CinematicRenderer). hyperframes: HTML and GSAP compositions (kinetic type, promos, launch reels, website-to-video, beat-timed music pieces). ffmpeg: cutting and joining footage; as a stand-in for animation it is a downgrade. When Remotion and HyperFrames are both installed, present both, each with one honest trade-off, recommend one and wait for the choice.

composition_mode.description: templated: the stock scene types in the stock compositions; fast and reliable, right for batches, variants, drafts and internal clips. atelier: a composition hand-authored for this piece from a written art direction; the recommendation for hero work, and slower to make. HyperFrames work is atelier by nature.

renderer_family.description: The creative grammar for templated work, from the pipeline's list. explainer-data, explainer-teacher, product-reveal, screen-demo and animation-first render with Explainer; cinematic-trailer and documentary-montage with CinematicRenderer; presenter with TalkingHead. Required when composition_mode is templated.

art_direction.description: Required for atelier: palette, type, motion character, layout system and one signature device used in one or two beats, written before any composition code; or the path of the note that holds it.

outputs.description: The deliverables: frame sizes, durations, platforms, languages.

scene_sources.description: Where each family of scenes comes from: supplied material, stock, generated images or video, or scenes the composition renders with no asset.

family.description: The scenes concerned, such as data beats, b-roll or product shots.

stages.description: Per-stage tool plan: which tools and providers each stage uses, whether they are configured, and the fallback.

role.description: What the tool does in this stage.

available.description: True when the tool's provider is configured now (capabilities).

approach.description: What happens in the stage and how.

quality_tradeoffs.description: Choices the operator should weigh, such as elevenlabs_tts against piper_tts, with what they gain or lose.

quality_impact.description: What the operator gains or loses.

alternative_paths.description: The free path in full, and what each paid upgrade changes in the result.

paid.description: True when the path includes any paid step.

taste_profile.description: A design read tied to audience, promise and platform ("investor-facing launch: precise, restrained, credible", never just "modern and clean"), three dials and what to avoid.

design_read.description: What the video should feel like for this brief, and why.

visual_variance.description: How much scenes may vary visually while staying coherent.

motion_intensity.description: How energetic the motion language is.

information_density.description: How much information can be on screen at once.

delivery_promise.description: What kind of video is promised. It is checked before rendering, so a still slideshow cannot pass for a motion-led video. The edit carries it unchanged into edit_decisions.

promise_type.description: motion_led: real motion carries the video. source_led: the supplied footage leads. data_explainer: data and charts carry it. teacher_explainer: a step-by-step walk through a concept. screen_demo: software or a website shown working. avatar_presenter: a presenter speaking to camera. hybrid: supplied footage with designed or generated support. localization: an existing video in another language.

motion_required.description: True when the video depends on real motion (video clips, animation), not on camera moves over stills.

source_required.description: True when the operator's supplied footage must lead.

tone_mode.description: Tone of the delivery, such as cinematic, educational, corporate, playful, raw, intimate or epic.

quality_floor.description: The lowest finish the operator accepts.

approved_fallback.description: A lesser form the operator agreed to if the promised one cannot be made: animatic or still_led. null (the default) when none was agreed.

voice.description: The narration voice: provider and voice, why it fits, delivery style and pace. A sample is approved before the full narration.

tool.description: edge_tts (free, needs the network), piper_tts (free, offline), openai_tts or elevenlabs_tts (paid); supplied for the operator's own recording or the speaker in the footage; none when the video has no narration.

voice_id.description: The voice name or id the tool takes.

rationale.description: Why this voice fits the brief.

delivery_style.description: Plain-language direction, such as warm expert, expressive narrator or crisp tutorial.

pacing_policy.description: How the voice uses pauses, speed and emphasis across the piece.

sample_approval_required.description: True when a voice sample must be approved before the full narration.

music_plan.description: Where the music comes from; mandatory whenever the video has sound. With no source, say so now, not at the asset stage.

source_type.description: user_library: a track from the operator's library (music_library). bring_your_own: a track the operator will provide. none: no music.

track_path.description: Path of the chosen track, when known.

notes.description: Where the music plays when not throughout, and anything else the mix must know.

method.description: composition: drawn word by word by the composition from the narration timing. burned: subtitle_gen cues burned in with ffmpeg_caption_burn. files: SRT or VTT files delivered beside the video only. none: no captions.

languages.description: Caption languages, as language codes such as en or es.

name.description: What the deliverable is, for example main-16x9 or teaser-vertical.

language.description: Language code, such as en or es.

unavailable.description: Needs that a capability without a configured provider would serve, with the alternative offered.

alternative.description: The free or supplied alternative, or the question put to the operator.

paid_step.description: One step that calls a tool which may charge the operator's provider account. Announce it before the call; make a sample before any batch.

purpose.description: What the step makes and why it is worth paying for.

credit_note.description: The tool's credit note as describe gives it, for example "Uses your OpenAI API credits".

sample_first.description: True when one sample is made and approved before the batch.

quantity.description: How many calls the step makes, the sample included.

free_alternative.description: The free way to cover the same need, and what it changes in the result.

approval.description: The operator's answer at this approval point.

user_notes.description: The operator's answer and any changes asked for, in their words.
